title: Naive, Seasonal-Naive & Drift Baselines
interviewAnswer: Forecasting should start with naive baselines. Last-value, seasonal-naive and drift forecasts often perform surprisingly well; a complex model is useful only if it beats the baseline out-of-sample.
keyPoints: Baseline defines whether complexity adds value.
why: Naive, Seasonal-Naive & Drift Baselines appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Forecasting should start with naive baselines. Last-value, seasonal-naive and drift forecasts often perform surprisingly well; a complex model is useful only if it beats the baseline out-of-sample. Drift extrapolates average trend. Baseline defines whether complexity adds value. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Forecast next Monday’s sales using last Monday before evaluating ARIMA or a neural model.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Naive, Seasonal-Naive & Drift Baselines make?
How would you validate or debug Naive, Seasonal-Naive & Drift Baselines in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.

lab.goal: Build naive and seasonal-naive forecasts before complex models.
lab.buildIt:
import numpy as np
y=np.array([10,12,11,13,15,16,14,11,13,12,14,16,17,15],float)
h=7
last=np.repeat(y[-1],h)
seasonal=y[-7:]
print('last',last,'seasonal',seasonal)
lab.shipIt: Ship a seasonal-naive fallback beside every forecasting service; if the complex model cannot beat it by segment/horizon, revisit the model or data.

visual.title: Forecast baselines
visual.caption: Always beat a simple naive/seasonal-naive baseline before adding model complexity.
